area: Combat readability & game feel (enemy telegraphs, parry/dash timing, camera, parry feedback, combat markers)

issues.title: Enemy warning cue (blade glint + swing SFX) arrives after human reaction time
issues.evidence: Enemy.cs:461 fires BladeGlint and plays a.sfx when stepNorm >= activeStart-0.18 (normalized, so its length depends on the clip). Python replica of TickAttack (phaseA/combat/telegraph_sim.py, 60 fps, Snappy(0.85,1.35)) gives glint-to-strike leads: ninja Attack1 0.183 s, Attack2 0.117 s, Attack3 0.150 s; elite 0.10-0.15 s; sumo Slap1 0.117 s, Slap2 0.183 s; Mizuchi 0.08-0.13 s; Ōzeki 0.12/0.18 s. The parry only works if pressed within [strike-0.24, strike] (PlayerController.cs:414, parryWindow 0.24). Monte Carlo with visual RT N(0.27,0.05) gives 0-4% reactive parry success on all common enemies (reaction_mc.txt, lead_times_chart.png). enemy_swing_1..3.wav peak 0.11-0.13 s after onset, i.e. on the hit, so it is not a warning. The danger SFX (danger_1.wav) is 3.72 s long and peaks 0.45 s after onset, unrelated to the strike time.
issues.fix: Replace the normalized glint with a time-based tell that starts when the attack step starts (ensō ring, steps 1-2 of the plan). Enforce minimum wind-ups: light opener 0.55 s, chained 0.42 s, heavy 0.65/0.50 s, unblockable 0.80 s, Kage 0.48/0.38 s. Add a hyōshigi tick at strike-0.30 s and move enemy_swing to the release so its peak lands on the hit.

issues.title: The 'telegraph' hold is mostly lost and happens mid-swing
issues.evidence: Enemy.cs:448 holdEnd = telegraph + (activeStart-0.12)*stepLen assumes clip rate 1, but the wind-up runs at 0.85 (EnemyArchetypes.Hit uses Snappy(0.85,...)), so most of the hold is consumed before the hold zone is reached. Measured hold: ninja Attack1 telegraph 0.12 s -> 0.03 s; Gorō Combo1 0.20 -> 0.10 s; Mizuchi a1 0.08 -> 0.00 s. The hold zone (stepNorm >= activeStart-0.12) is in the middle of the swing, not at the wind-up apex, so the pause shows a moving weapon. EstimateStrikeEta (Enemy.cs:490-501) is an approximation of this same flawed model.
issues.fix: New deterministic step timeline (plan step 1): AttackDef.apex (normalized wind-up apex), AttackDef.windup (s), releaseRate. Anticipation runs to the apex, holds at the apex for max(0, windupMin - natural), then a fast release to activeStart. Drive Animator speed from the piecewise curve so StrikeEta = T - stepClock is exact. Delete the holdEnd logic.

issues.title: Gorō's damage frames land before the visible hammer impact (up to 0.65 s early)
issues.evidence: Blender analysis of Assets/Models/Minijefe.fbx (hammer Cylinder.005 parented to bone BaseM, farthest-vertex speed per frame at 30 fps; phaseA/combat/blender/goro_impact.json). Combo1: fast swing n=0.64-0.83 (peak 0.69) vs activeStart 0.48 (EnemyArchetypes.cs:128), about 0.19 s before the hammer moves. Combo3: swing 0.62-0.73 vs 0.45 (0.15 s early). Heavy slam: swing 0.73-0.75, ground contact 0.78, vs 0.55, so the shockwave fires about 0.65 s before the hammer lands. Combo2 0.51-0.54 vs 0.50 is fine. The goro_Combo1/Combo3/Heavy contact sheets confirm the hammer is still cocked over the shoulder at the damage frame.
issues.fix: EnemyArchetypes.Goro: c1 activeStart/End 0.66/0.80 (apex 0.58), c2 0.52/0.62 (apex 0.42), c3 0.63/0.74 (apex 0.55), slam 0.77/0.80 (apex ~0.68), spin unchanged. Add an editor validator (acceptance test T3) that samples clips and checks activeStart against weapon-speed peaks, so new clips from the animation pass can't regress.

issues.title: Common sumo 'Embestida imparable' never moves (charge only exists in Boss)
issues.evidence: Boss.cs:197-209 implements the 'charge' special. A regular sumo is spawned as a plain Enemy (CharacterFactory.cs:246-252 adds Boss only for goro/mizuchi/ozeki/kage). Enemy.TickSpecial (Enemy.cs:504) just calls TryHitPlayer with range 2.4. The attack has lunge 0 (EnemyArchetypes.cs:95) and the pattern requires minRange 3.5 (line 101), so the sumo plays the near-static Special clip in place and can never connect. It still fires DangerTelegraph, the 危 marker and the 'danger' sound, and StoryDirector.cs:277-288 can start the one-time 'press Dash' slow-mo tutorial for this attack.
issues.fix: Move the 'charge' and 'slam' cases (and the charge branch of ComputeStrikeEta) from Boss into Enemy, so every enemy can use them. Show a charge lane telegraph. Gate the dash tutorial on an attack that can actually connect (charge with a lane toward Kaito).

issues.title: Sumo attack and idle clips have no visible anticipation (nearly static)
issues.evidence: Silhouette XOR metric over the clip contact sheets (phaseA/combat/motion_metric.txt): sumo_Attack1 16.5%, Attack2 8.1%, Attack3 39.7%, Special 9.6%, Idle 0.0%, Exhausted 0.0%. For comparison: goro_Combo1 89.8%, ninja_Attack1 111%. The sumo also has no weapon, so the glint falls back to AimPoint+forward*0.6 and there is no trail. ninja_Attack2 is 7.4%: only the 3 px katana moves, the body is static.
issues.fix: Short term: EnemyMotion procedural anticipation (plan step 4; lean back / crouch / coil during wind-up, then a snap-forward stretch at release; sumo amount 1.6). Long term: the animation pass must author real anticipation keys (wind-up apex poses held 2-4 frames) for every attack clip, and update AttackDef.apex accordingly.

issues.title: Attackers are near-invisible: dark bodies, 3 px katana, 5-frame glint, camouflaged on the lake
issues.evidence: Camera model (cam_pixels.py, CameraDirector params) at 1080p: ninja 113 px (combat, no lock, ~20.4 m), 134 px (lock d=3), 75 px (boss framing 31 m). finisher_prompt2.png measures ≈137 px. A 0.75 m katana is 75-88 px long but ~3 px thick, dark blue. CharacterFactory.BlackFloor = 0.13, so ninjas are near-black. In finisher_prompt.png three ninjas fighting in shadow are invisible; only their HP bars show. FXManager.BladeGlint uses flashWhite (FXFactory life 0.09 s, scale 0.5): 5 frames at 60 fps. boss_mizuchi5.png: white/cyan water sparkles are the same color as the glint and the wave FX.
issues.fix: Ground ensō with a dark ink underlay (readable on night ground, snow and water: mock_enso_tell.png, mock_enso_snow.png). Stroke width clamped to ≥ 10-12 px in screen space. Emissive weapon glow plus a per-attacker TellLight that builds during the wind-up. Eye glint at the close. Tighter combat camera (step 9).

issues.title: Unblockable attacks have no countdown; dash i-frames are only 0.22 s
issues.evidence: Enemy.cs:430-440 calls OnUnblockableTelegraph at step start: red sprite, red light 0.4 s, 危 marker 1.0 s, danger sound. Simulated strike follows 0.65 s (sumo charge), 1.88 s (Gorō slam), 0.70 s (spin), 0.53 s (Kage windslash). Dash i-frames are 0.02-0.24 s after press (PlayerConfig dashIFrameStart/End). The red glint lead (0.43-0.65 s) does not line up with the i-frames either. Simulated reactive dodge: Gorō slam 7%, spin 0%.
issues.fix: Crimson serrated ensō plus the real hit area (slam disc, spin disc, charge/windslash lane) filling in sync, closing at strike-0.12 s so a press at the close centres the i-frames on the hit. A taiko onset sound replaces the 3.7 s danger clip. Tick at strike-0.36 s.

issues.title: Kanji in combat markers and the tutorial (user explicitly rejects them)
issues.evidence: UIManager.cs:395 ShowDanger '危'; :396 ShowGuardMark '防'; :323 guard status '<color=#9fc8ff>防</color>'; :347 finisher prompt '[F] 処刑 Ejecutar'; StoryDirector.cs:285 '¡Golpe imparable (危)!'. Visible in finisher_prompt.png / finisher_prompt2.png. (HUD 命/魂/怒 and seals 山水竹 belong to the HUD audit.)
issues.fix: Remove all glyph markers. Danger = crimson ring + procedural red brush-diamond sprite above the pips. Guard = steel-blue ground crescent in front of the enemy. Finisher = '[F] Ejecutar'. Tutorial text refers to 'el anillo rojo'. Add a CJK-regex acceptance test.

issues.title: Kaito cannot parry or dash during most of his own swing
issues.evidence: PlayerController.Combat.cs:82-85: earlyCancel only while attackNorm < activeStart*0.7, lateCancel from cancelWindow (0.55-0.6). Locked: Corte 1 attackNorm 0.196-0.55 (≈0.15 s); Corte final 0.14-0.60 of a 0.667 s clip (≈0.31 s). With tells that start 0.4-0.85 s before the strike, the player will often see the tell while attacking and be unable to respond.
issues.fix: earlyCancel = attackNorm < a.activeStart; lateCancel = attackNorm > min(a.cancelWindow, a.activeEnd). Parry/dash are then blocked only while the blade is actually cutting. Keep input buffering so a press during the active frames fires at activeEnd.

issues.title: Parry state is invisible and whiffs give no feedback, so timing can't be learned
issues.evidence: ParryStance = TrueBlock.anim, 0.10 s, 3.5% silhouette change (kaito_ParryStance.png), while the window is 0.24 s. When the window expires, TickParry goes silently to ParryRecover for 0.28 s (PlayerController.Combat.cs:228-246). A hit during recover just shows damage, with no early/late distinction.
issues.fix: ParryCrescent VFX lasting exactly CurrentParryWindow (gold during the perfect part), stance held on its last frame. Grey crescent break + 'parry_whiff' sound on expiry. 'Pronto' label if a parryable hit lands ≤ 0.35 s after a whiff; 'Tarde' label if parry is pressed ≤ 0.20 s after being hit; first 12 times (save counter). Request a 2-frame guard pose from the animation pass.

issues.title: Parry feedback darkens the scene instead of lighting it up
issues.evidence: OnParrySuccess perfect: Game.Time.SlowMotion(0.3, 0.45) (PlayerController.Combat.cs:268). ScreenFX.cs:116/126 sets saturation = Base - (1-timeScale)*45 ≈ -31 during it. FXManager.ParryFlash: light 10 intensity, range 9 m, 0.25 s. Design doc: the parry should LIGHT UP the scene. Hit-stop is global for both normal (0.07 s) and perfect (0.11 s) parries, which also freezes other attackers in group fights.
issues.fix: ScreenFX.ParryLight: postExposure +0.9 EV (perfect) / +0.4 (normal) with ~0.09 s exponential decay, bloom +2.5/+1.0, vignette -0.12, saturation +12. Parry slow-mo excluded from the desaturation. Flash light 28 intensity / 14 m (perfect), 12 / 9 m (normal). Moon intensity x1.5 for 0.12 s. Gold ink burst from the attacker's ensō. Perfect slow-mo 0.25x for 0.30 s. Normal parry uses local freeze on both fighters instead of a global hit-stop.

issues.title: Two attackers can strike almost simultaneously
issues.evidence: CombatDirector.cs:43-49: maxAttackers 2, and the only spacing is 0.6 s between token grants. The actual strike time depends on approach distance, clip and lunge, so two strikes can land < 0.2 s apart. ParrySuccess auto-parries only hits within 0.18 s (PlayerController.cs:420), and between 0.18 and ~0.4 s the second press is very hard.
issues.fix: CombatDirector.ReserveStrike(enemy, naturalTime): keeps the scheduled strike times of other attackers ≥ 0.42 s apart (minions vs boss ≥ 0.5 s) by extending the apex hold (≤ 0.6 s), otherwise delays the attack start.

issues.title: Camera too far in boss fights and no off-screen threat indicator
issues.evidence: CameraDirector.cs:29-32/306/318/325: combat 18-28 m, lock 15.5+0.6d, boss +3 m. Unlocked boss framing reaches 31 m: Kaito 66 px, ninja 75 px, and the ensō stroke would be 3 px (mock_enso_snow.png, boss_goro3.png). At 20 m the visible ground half-depth is ≈7 m, so Estocada (5.5 m lunge), sumo charge (11 m), windslash (10 m) and Mizuchi waves can start off-screen. Enemies hidden behind trees/roofs are not handled (Occluder only clears what blocks Kaito).
issues.fix: Pitch 45, combat 15-23 m, lock Clamp(14+0.55d, 14.5, 23), boss extra = Clamp(0.9*(bossHeight-1.7), 0, 2.5). Threat framing pulls focus up to 25% toward an attacker mid-tell that is outside the safe area. -0.8° FOV only on heavy/unblockable tells. ThreatIndicators edge chevrons (plan step 10).

issues.title: World-space widget clutter competes with telegraphs
issues.evidence: finisher_prompt.png: three HP bars, pips, 防 and '¡DESEQUILIBRADO!' stacked over '[F] 処刑 Ejecutar' for clustered ninjas. Every engaged enemy shows a bar (UIManager.cs:299-301).
issues.fix: HP bars only for the lock target and enemies hit in the last 3 s. Pips stay for engaged enemies. Status text only on the lock target or nearest exhausted enemy. Resolve vertical overlaps by sorting on screen y and pushing overlapping widgets up 22 px.

issues.title: Poise deflect of Kaito's 3rd hit is untelegraphed
issues.evidence: Enemy.cs:616-626: ninja poiseHits 2, so the 3rd consecutive neutral hit of Kaito's 3-hit combo is always Guarded (Counter + Kaito Blocked). Nothing warns the player beforehand; '防' appears only after the deflect.
issues.fix: Show the steel-blue guard crescent as soon as neutralHits == poiseHits (next hit will bounce) and while State == Guard.

issues.title: Parryable projectiles (Mizuchi waves) have no timing cue
issues.evidence: Boss.cs:136 returns +inf StrikeEta for 'wave'. WaveProjectile hits at 1.1 m; kind Projectile is parryable (CombatTypes.cs:34). The wave FX is cyan/white on sparkling water.
issues.fix: Small closing gold ensō around Kaito's feet driven by the nearest on-course wave's ETA = (dist-1.1)/speed when ETA < 0.7 s. Report that ETA as StrikeEta so the bots/tests can use it.

issues.title: Enemy trail starts at the glint and looks the same for parryable and unblockable
issues.evidence: Enemy.cs:118 BladeTrail color (0.85,0.85,1,0.6); Enemy.cs:466 Begin at activeStart-0.18; lifetime 0.16 s (CharacterFX.cs:60).
issues.fix: Begin at release (hold end), lifetime 0.22 s, color by kind: warm white for parryable, crimson for unblockable.

plan:
GOAL: every damaging enemy action gives an honest, time-accurate warning starting ≥ 0.38-0.80 s before it lands. The warning reads on any ground at 1080p from the 45° camera, uses no glyphs, and is backed by sound. Parrying and dodging can be learned and are rewarded with a parry that lights up the scene. Order = dependency order.

STEP 0 - Data and bug fixes (small, do first)
0a. EnemyArchetypes.Goro (EnemyArchetypes.cs:128-134), from the Blender hammer-speed analysis:
- c1 activeStart/End 0.66/0.80
- c2 0.52/0.62
- c3 0.63/0.74
- slam 0.77/0.80
- spin unchanged
Hit() derives lungeStart = aStart-0.25 automatically.
0b. Move the 'charge' and 'slam' cases from Boss.TickSpecial into Enemy.TickSpecial (protected virtual, shared), and the charge branch of Boss.ComputeStrikeEta into Enemy.ComputeStrikeEta. The common sumo then actually charges (speed specialParam 11 m/s, DustTrail). Boss keeps its overrides for teleport, summon, clones, wave, windslash and spin.
0c. StoryDirector.cs:277-288: trigger the dash tutorial only for unblockables that can connect (charge lane toward Kaito or slam with Kaito inside the radius), and only at tell progress ≥ 0.6.

STEP 1 - Deterministic attack timeline (Enemies/Enemy.cs, Combat/CombatTypes.cs)
1a. New AttackDef fields:
- apex [0..1]: wind-up apex, the weapon fully cocked; -1 = auto max(0, activeStart-0.15)
- windup (s): minimum time from step start to strike; 0 = default by role
- releaseRate = 1.6 (clip-rate multiplier from apex to activeStart)
- tellBias: default 0.06 s parryable, 0.12 s unblockable
The old 'telegraph' field becomes extra windup (windup += telegraph) for compatibility.
1b. Initial apex values:
- ninja Attack1 0.50, Attack2 0.28, Attack3 0.38
- Gorō Combo1 0.58, Combo2 0.42, Combo3 0.55, Heavy 0.68, Spin 0.15
- Kaito clips (used by Kage) Attack1 0.20, Attack2 0.15, Attack3 0.12
- sumo: activeStart-0.12 (its clips have no apex; procedural anticipation in step 4)
1c. Default windup minimum (step 0 = opener, step > 0 = chained):
- Light 0.55 / 0.42
- Heavy 0.65 / 0.50
- Unblockable 0.80
- Estocada 0.70
- Guard counter (StartAttack(true)) ≥ 0.50
- Kage 0.48 / 0.38, windslash 0.80
- Boss phase ≥ 1: x0.9, floor 0.38
1d. New pure struct StepTimeline (Enemies/StepTimeline.cs), unit-testable. Build(AttackDef a, float clipLen, int stepIndex, int phase, float extraHold) returns:
- tA = apex*clipLen/0.85
- tR = (activeStart-apex)*clipLen/releaseRate
- hold = max(0, windupMin - (tA+tR)) + extraHold
- T = tA + hold + tR
- tellStart = max(0, T - tellMax), with tellMax 0.85 s parryable / 1.0 s unblockable
- NormAt(t): ease-out 0 -> apex over [0,tA]; apex -> apex+0.01 over the hold (breathing); ease-in apex -> activeStart over tR; then rate 1.0 to the end of the clip.
1e. Enemy.BeginStep builds the timeline and asks CombatDirector.ReserveStrike (step 6) for extraHold. TickAttack:
- stepClock += dt unless anim.Frozen; stepNorm = NormAt(stepClock).
- Animator speed = (NormAt(stepClock+dt)-stepNorm)/dt*clipLen, clamped 0..4. Correct drift against GetCurrentAnimatorStateInfo(0).normalizedTime when not in transition: if |diff| > 0.04, add 6*diff.
- strikeEta = T - stepClock (exact).
- Lunge runs over [tA+hold, T+0.05*clipLen].
- Tracking (Face target) runs until release starts (tA+hold), so a sidestep after the release is real counterplay.
- Remove the holdEnd/holding code and EstimateStrikeEta.
Expose:
- public float TellStart, StrikeTime (both in stepClock)
- public float TellProgress01 = clamp01((stepClock - tellStart)/(T - tellBias - tellStart))
- public bool InTell
- public AttackKind StepKind
- public Vector3 HitAreaCenter, HitAreaSize (for specials)
Keep AboutToStrike (StrikeWarning 0.18) for AutoPilot and tutorials; it is now exact.

STEP 2 - Ensō attack tell (new FX/AttackTell.cs + FXManager.BeginTell/EndTell)
2a. Pool of 6 AttackTell objects in FXManager. Enemy.BeginStep calls Game.FX.BeginTell(this) when the step damages (damage > 0, or special charge/slam/spin/windslash). Enemy calls EndTell(this, outcome) on strike, parry (OnParried), stagger, death, phase change or Scripted. Outcomes: Struck, Parried, Cancelled.
2b. Geometry: procedural ring mesh, 96 segments, rebuilt per frame only for the active arc.
- radius = enemy.Radius + 0.55 m (bosses + 0.7)
- stroke width = max(0.10 m, 12 px * metersPerPixel), where metersPerPixel = 2*camDist*tan(fov/2)/Screen.height
- start angle = direction from enemy to Kaito; sweeps clockwise as seen from the camera; fraction f = TellProgress01
- width taper over the first 6% and at the head; bright additive dot (0.25 m) at the stroke head
Two layers:
- dark ink underlay: alpha blend, #120A0C, a 0.55, width x1.6 (contrast on snow, lake, torch light)
- top stroke: FXMaterials.Additive with vertex colors
Ground conform: raycast down at the centre, align to the ground normal, y +0.05, ZTest LEqual (characters occlude it), no shadows. Brush texture: procedural 256x32 dry-brush strip with noise in alpha along u.
2c. Parryable look: gold #FFD678 -> white #FFFFF0 as f -> 1. At f = 1 (= strike - 0.06 s): flash width x1.8, alpha 1, 0.08 s, then faint until the hit, fade 0.15 s after it.
- Parried: stroke shatters into 8 arcs flying outward (0.2 s) + gold RingWave 2.5 m + gold ink flecks.
- Cancelled: ink dissolve, 0.12 s.
2d. Unblockable look: crimson #EB281E, width x1.4, serrated (12 teeth, alternate segments x1.6 width), closes at strike - 0.12 s. Hit area filled in sync (alpha 0.18 -> 0.35, filling from the centre):
- slam: disc of radius specialParam at position + forward*max(0.5, range*0.4)
- spin: disc of radius range
- charge: lane of width 2*Radius+0.6, length min(dist+2, 9 m); tracks until release, then freezes
- windslash: lane 2.8 m x specialParam
Head icon: procedural red brush-diamond Image placed above the pips. No text.
2e. Guard vocabulary (same component, GuardArc mode): steel-blue #9FC8FF 120° crescent, radius Radius+0.6, alpha 0.5, in front of the enemy facing Kaito. Shown while State == Guard, for 0.7 s on a Counter, and when neutralHits == poiseHits.
Keep the vocabulary to three meanings: a gold ring being drawn means parry on close; a red serrated ring plus a red area means dash out on close; a blue crescent means your hits will bounce. Exhausted keeps pips + finisher prompt (no ring).
2f. Settings.TellMode {Full, Subtle, Off} (PlayerPrefs 'nindo.tells', added to the Options panel). Subtle shows only the last 0.25 s (complete ring flash) plus audio. TellStyle static class holds all colors, widths and biases for designers.

STEP 3 - Body and weapon cues (inside AttackTell or FX/TellBodyCue.cs)
3a. Weapon glow: CharacterFactory caches an emissive clone of each weapon material (the KatanaRig renderer; Gorō Cylinder.005). During the tell, MaterialPropertyBlock _EmissionColor ramps intensity 0 -> 3 (HDR) by f; warm white for parryable, red for unblockable. Bloom threshold 0.95 makes the 3 px katana a bright readable line.
- Sumo: two additive glow sprites (0.35 m) parented to the hand bones (search 'Mano'/'Hand').
3b. TellLight: pool of 3 point lights, no shadows, at AimPoint + 0.6 m toward the camera, range 3.5, intensity 0 -> 4 following f. Colors: parryable (1, 0.9, 0.7), unblockable (1, 0.25, 0.15). Off 0.1 s after the strike.
3c. Eye/blade glint (star sprite, 2 frames) at the close moment, aligned to the parry moment, replacing today's BladeGlint timing.
3d. Enemy BladeTrail: Begin at release (stepClock >= tA+hold) instead of activeStart-0.18, lifetime 0.22 s, color by kind.

STEP 4 - Procedural anticipation (new Enemies/EnemyMotion.cs)
Insert a pivot between the enemy root and the model, like ProceduralMotion does for Kaito, so Boss spin and DeathRoutine (which rotate the model) keep working. Channels driven by the timeline:
- Wind-up [0, tA+hold]: ease to lean back -8°*amount around local right, scaleY 0.95 / XZ 1.03, yaw coil -10°.
- Hold: 9 Hz, 0.6° tremble.
- Release: spring (ω=28, critically damped) to +7° forward and scaleY 1.04, then neutral in 0.25 s.
EnemyConfig.anticipation: ninja 1.0, sumo 1.6, Gorō 0.5, Kage 0.8. Drop to 0.3 (secondary motion) once the animation pass delivers authored anticipation keys.

STEP 5 - Audio cues (NindoContent sfx via Tools/Unity/generate_assets.py)
New keys:
- tell_light: blade 'shing' at tellStart for parryable light attacks
- tell_heavy: lower shing + cloth whoosh, for heavy attacks
- tell_danger: taiko 'don' at tellStart for unblockables; replaces the 3.72 s danger_1.wav in OnUnblockableTelegraph
- tell_tick: hyōshigi wood clack at strike - 0.30 s (parryable) / - 0.36 s (unblockable); played 2D (spatialBlend 0) when the attacker is the lock target or within 8 m; volume 0.8
Move enemy_swing to the release so its 0.11-0.13 s peak lands on the hit. Placeholder synthesized WAVs: scratch phaseA/combat/audio_proto/. Replace them with proper foley before shipping.

STEP 6 - Strike scheduler (Combat/CombatDirector.cs)
public float ReserveStrike(Enemy e, float naturalAbsTime, bool chained):
- keep a list of (enemy, absolute strike time) for the next 3 s
- return the extra hold needed so the strike is ≥ minStrikeSpacing (0.42 s) from any other enemy's strike (0.5 s between a boss and its minions)
- the enemy's own combo steps are exempt
- if the extra hold would be > 0.6 s, StartAttack returns to Strafe and retries in 0.3 s
Release the entry on EndTell.

STEP 7 - Player side (Player/PlayerController.Combat.cs, PlayerConfig.cs, new FX/ParryCrescent)
7a. TickAttack cancels: earlyCancel = attackNorm < a.activeStart; lateCancel = attackNorm > Mathf.Min(a.cancelWindow, a.activeEnd). Parry and Dash are buffered through the active frames.
7b. StartParry spawns a ParryCrescent in front of Kaito (150°, radius 0.9 m, height 0.9 m) living CurrentParryWindow; gold during the first perfectWindow*parryWindowMul, steel white after. Play ParryStance and freeze it on its last frame after 0.05 s until the window ends.
7c. On whiff (TickParry expiry): crescent breaks grey + 'parry_whiff' sound. Timing coach:
- if a parryable hit lands ≤ 0.35 s after a whiff, show a small world label 'Pronto' above Kaito
- if parry is pressed ≤ 0.20 s after taking a parryable hit, show 'Tarde'
- only for the first 12 occurrences (SaveData counter 'tip_timing'), always in a future practice mode
7d. Keep parryWindow 0.24, perfectWindow 0.11, parryRecover 0.28, spamPenalty 0.55. Once the cues are readable, these values are fair.

STEP 8 - Parry and hit juice (FX/ScreenFX.cs, FX/FXManager.cs, Core/TimeController.cs, World/WorldBuilder.cs)
8a. ScreenFX.ParryLight(bool perfect):
- postExposure +0.9 EV / +0.4 EV, decaying exp(-t/0.09)
- bloom.intensity +2.5 / +1.0
- vignette -0.12
- saturation +12 for 0.25 s
Tag parry slow-mo (a SlowMotion overload with a 'noDesaturate' flag) so ScreenFX.cs:116/126 ignores it.
8b. FXManager.ParryFlash: perfect FlashLight(28, range 14, 0.22 s, warm white); normal FlashLight(12, 9 m, 0.15 s). WorldBuilder exposes Moon; its intensity goes x1.5 for 0.12 s on a perfect parry. Clash sparks at the midpoint between the two blades.
8c. Perfect parry: global HitStop 0.10 s + SlowMotion(0.25, 0.30). Normal parry: local freeze of Kaito and the attacker (CharacterAnimator.Freeze 0.07 s) instead of a global hit-stop.

STEP 9 - Camera (Camera/CameraDirector.cs)
- combatPitch 47 -> 45
- combatDistanceMin 18 -> 15, combatDistanceMax 28 -> 23
- lock targetDist = Clamp(14 + d*0.55, 14.5, 23)
- bossExtraDistance -> Clamp(0.9*(boss.config.height*scale - 1.7), 0, 2.5)

DESIGN PRINCIPLES
1. Honest telegraphs: the ring always closes on the real hit. Bosses may vary the hold (Kage phase 2 ±0.15 s random hold, Gorō delayed slam) and the ring shows the delay. Difficulty comes from mixups, rhythm changes and parryable vs unblockable reads, not from unreadable timing.
2. One visual language for parryable/unblockable/guard, distinguishable by shape and motion as well as color (colorblind-safe).
3. All cues run on scaled game time, so slow-mo and hit-stop keep them in sync.
4. Coordinate with the animation pass: new clips must keep apex/activeStart metadata. Add an editor tool that auto-detects them: apex = slowest weapon frame before the speed peak, activeStart = first frame above 50% of peak speed.
